rules.title: The interface indicates where the user is
rules.description: The current location is indicated within the navigation structure, and the indication is not carried by color alone.
rules.rationale: Orientation is a precondition for navigation. A user who cannot tell where they are cannot form an intention about where to go.
rules.remediation: Mark the current item in the navigation, both visually and programmatically.
rules.$assuranceNote: The indication depends on rendered state per route, so it is established for the routes a browser run visited.

rules.title: Meaningful application states are addressable
rules.description: A state a user would want to return to, share, or bookmark has an address, and that address stays stable. Back behaves the way the platform's back behaves.
rules.rationale: A state with no address cannot be shared, restored, or returned to after a reload. The user's only recovery is to reproduce the sequence that reached it.
rules.remediation: Represent meaningful state in the route, and keep route shapes stable across releases.
rules.$assuranceNote: Declared routes are enumerable from source. Which application states deserve an address is a design decision no scan makes.

rules.title: Navigation away from unsaved work is protected
rules.description: Leaving a view with unsaved changes either preserves them or warns before discarding them.
rules.rationale: Silent loss of work is indistinguishable from a bug and unrecoverable either way, and it is usually caused by a navigation the user did not realize was destructive.
rules.remediation: Persist the draft, or intercept the navigation and say what will be lost.
rules.$assuranceNote: Source can show that a guard is registered. Whether it fires on every path out of the view is a runtime property.
